title: Dhamaal 4 Made ₹22 Crore on Saturday. Nobody Saw That Coming.
excerpt: A 64% jump from opening day, half a million BookMyShow tickets, and Ajay Devgn's biggest comedy weekend in years. The franchise just reminded Bollywood who really owns the multiplex.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Dhamaal 4 earned ₹22 crore on Saturday, a 64% increase from its opening day.
  • The film sold over 500,000 tickets on BookMyShow within two days.
  • Mumbai and Chennai reported occupancy rates of 67% and 85% respectively during night shows.
  • Trade projections estimate an opening weekend gross of over ₹60 crore.
  • The film is resonating with audiences both in India and overseas.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=IG-eByZdz6Y Here is what a word-of-mouth explosion looks like in real time: on Friday morning, **Dhamaal 4** opened to cautious optimism and a decent ₹13.72 crore. By Saturday night, it had collected ₹22.47 crore — a staggering 64% jump — and crossed half a million tickets on BookMyShow alone. The theatres weren't just full. They were *vibrating*. https://www.instagram.com/p/DamVWGno3zp/ Let those numbers settle. In a summer crowded with **Cocktail 2**, **Welcome to the Jungle**, and **Alpha**, a comedy franchise that started in 2007 as an unofficial riff on *It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World* just delivered the kind of Saturday surge that gives trade analysts heart palpitations. Total India net after two days: ₹36.50 crore. Worldwide gross: ₹53.80 crore. And Sunday hasn't even finished yet. ## The Saturday That Changed Everything ![Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2b/Mumbai_Bandra-Worli_Sea_Link.jpg) > **"Taran Adarsh gave it 3.5 stars and called it "MAZEDAAR" — which, coming from Adarsh, is practically a standing ovation."** The signs were there by morning. Between 9 AM and 10 AM on Saturday, Dhamaal 4 sold 13,870 tickets on BookMyShow — more than double the 6,770 in the same window on Friday. By afternoon, occupancy had jumped from 8.38% on opening morning to 33.92%. Mumbai hit 41% overall, Lucknow touched 45%, and Chennai — Chennai! — recorded a jaw-dropping 58.5%. The evening and night shows were where it got obscene. Mumbai night shows hit 67% occupancy. Ahmedabad: 70%. Chennai: 85%. These are numbers that belong to a tentpole action film, not a comedy about treasure-hunting pirates. Taran Adarsh gave it 3.5 stars and called it "MAZEDAAR" — which, coming from Adarsh, is practically a standing ovation. The BMS audience rating sits at 8.9 out of 10 from over 4,200 votes. When the audience score is that high and the Saturday jump is that violent, you're looking at a film that's going to run for weeks. ## The Franchise That Refuses to Age This is the fourth Dhamaal film in 19 years. The first three collectively grossed approximately ₹355 crore. **Total Dhamaal** in 2019 alone did ₹154 crore lifetime. The franchise has survived changing tastes, the OTT revolution, and the post-pandemic theatrical reset — and here it is, posting one of the biggest comedy weekends of 2026. **Ajay Devgn**, **Riteish Deshmukh**, and **Arshad Warsi** return as the chaotic trio, this time joined by **Ravi Kishan**, **Sanjeeda Shaikh**, and **Esha Gupta**. Director **Indra Kumar** has ditched the road-trip formula for sea pirates and supernatural elements as the gang chases a ₹50 crore treasure. The CBFC passed it with zero cuts and a UA 13+ rating — a clean, wide-access entertainer that's filling up family shows in a way Bollywood desperately needs. ## Leading Overseas, Too ![Chennai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/32/Chennai_Central.jpg)

The diaspora is showing up. In Australia, Dhamaal 4 collected 84,000 AUD on opening day, ahead of both Cocktail 2 (77,600 AUD) and Welcome to the Jungle (51,000 AUD). In New Zealand, it led with 46,000 NZD — more than double Welcome to the Jungle's 21,000 NZD. Total overseas gross after two days: ₹10 crore. For NRIs who grew up quoting "Yeh Baburao ka style hai" and making their friends watch the original on pirated DVDs, the fourth installment is hitting the nostalgia button hard. And the fact that it's playing wide in Australian and New Zealand multiplexes says something about where the Hindi comedy audience lives now. ## What's Next Trade projections now peg the opening weekend at ₹60 crore-plus, with eyes on Akshay Kumar's **Welcome to the Jungle** (₹65.83 crore) for a top-three weekend finish in 2026. That's behind only **Dhurandhar 2** and **Border 2** — both massive action spectacles, not comedies. If Dhamaal 4 crosses that ₹65 crore mark this weekend, it won't just be a box office story. It'll be a statement: Bollywood comedies can still open big, grow bigger, and fill theatres without a single explosion or patriotic speech. Sometimes all you need is Ajay Devgn, a ghost, and a treasure map.
